data.title: IPA Capital Markets Arranges $50 Million in Financing for 18-Property Industrial Portfolio
data.description:
IPA Capital Markets, a division of Marcus & Millichap () specializing in capital markets services for major private and institutional clients, announced today that Frank Montalto, managing director, and Ethan Splan, director, both based in the firm’s Chicago office, arranged $50 million in financing for an 18-property industrial portfolio located across Texas, Oklahoma and Georgia.

The non-recourse loan features a five-year term, a 70% loan-to-value ratio, a 6.75% interest rate and interest-only payments throughout the loan term.

“This financing reflects the continued strength of well-located industrial assets and the durability of lender demand for stabilized portfolios with strong fundamentals,” said Montalto. “We were pleased to secure non-recourse financing with competitive leverage and pricing that supports the sponsor’s long-term business plan across these markets.”

About IPA Capital Markets

IPA Capital Markets is a division of Marcus & Millichap (). IPA Capital Markets provides major private and institutional clients with commercial real estate capital markets financing solutions, including debt, mezzanine financing, preferred and joint venture equity, and sponsor equity. For more information, please visit institutionalpropertyadvisors.com/capital-markets

About Marcus & Millichap, Inc. ()

Marcus & Millichap, Inc. is a leading brokerage firm specializing in commercial real estate investment sales, financing, research and advisory services with offices throughout the United States and Canada. Marcus & Millichap closed 8,818 transactions with a sales volume of $50.8 billion in 2025. The company had 1,808 investment sales and financing professionals in more than 80 offices who provide investment brokerage and financing services to sellers and buyers of commercial real estate at year end. data.title: Sequoia-backed chip startup Nuvacore raising funds at about a $2.5 billion valuation, sources say
data.description:
Key points:
  • Funding round seeks hundreds of millions of dollars, two people familiar say
  • Round has not closed and valuation and capital amount could change
  • Silicon Valley investors have revived their interest in hardware companies

By Max A. Cherney and Krystal Hu

Six-month-old microchip startup Nuvacore, which does not yet have a product, is raising hundreds of millions of dollars at a roughly $2.5 billion valuation to develop a new central processor designed for data centers, according to two people familiar with the fundraising.

Nuvacore is seeking to raise the funds as the appetite for central processors has swollen due to the thirst for data-crunching capacity to power chatbots such as Anthropic's Claude. CPUs perform vital functions as traffic controllers for Nvidia's AI chips and run autonomous AI software known as agents.

The roughly $2.5 billion valuation has not been previously reported. The Information reported previously that Nuvacore was raising $200 million or more. The funding round has not closed, and the people cautioned that the valuation and size of the capital raise could change.

Intel and Advanced Micro Devices , which use x86 technology, have long dominated the data center CPU market. Companies designing chips based on Arm's technology — found inside Amazon and Microsoft custom CPUs — have also attempted to make inroads in the data center market.

Nuvacore has not yet developed a product. Last month, it described an unconventional design strategy: to build the core functionality of the chip before committing to an architecture such as the x86 used by Intel and AMD, or Arm, which is used in most mobile phones.

The design strategy will allow the company's engineers to avoid the limitations and requirements of specific architectures and optimize a design for the type of computations that are most common in data centers and AI infrastructure, Nuvacore said.

Nuvacore declined to comment.

The San Jose, California-based startup was founded by renowned engineers Gerard Williams, John Bruno and Ram Srinivasan. Williams, a former Apple executive, sold a prior startup called Nuvia to Qualcomm for $1.4 billion in 2021.

Nuvacore earlier this year announced a seed funding round led by Sequoia Capital. It joins a series of young chip startups that have sought billion-dollar valuations before releasing a product as investor appetite for AI hardware companies has returned.

Over the past decade, Silicon Valley venture capital firms have taken much less interest in hardware than software because of hardware's longer development cycles, higher capital needs and the industry's cyclical demand.

Investors put about $10.7 billion into semiconductor startups in the first five months of 2026, already outpacing the $12.2 billion raised globally in all of 2025, according to Crunchbase data.

Earlier this year, Intel said it could not manufacture enough chips to meet demand, and was able to sell products it had previously determined were too faulty for sale. AMD also described swelling CPU sales in a recent results conference call with analysts.

Shares in both companies have risen more than 180% this year.

Nvidia launched a CPU called Vera this year. CEO Jensen Huang has said the company expects to sell $20 billion worth of its Vera CPU in this fiscal year, which ends in January.

data.title: Kalshi probes suspicious trades tied to Trump press secretary pick, WSJ reports
data.description:
Prediction market Kalshi has launched an investigation into suspicious trades tied to the selection of Katie Zacharia as U.S. President Donald Trump's new White House press secretary, the Wall Street Journal reported on Friday, citing a company spokesperson.

Kalshi declined to comment on the report.

Here are some details:

  • At least three small wagers were placed before news of Zacharia's selection emerged, potentially netting traders thousands of dollars in profits, the Journal reported.

  • A $19 bet placed late on Thursday is set to pay $1,896, while wagers of about $74 and $80 placed on Friday are expected to pay $3,689 and $4,023, respectively.

  • Zacharia, a conservative commentator who previously worked briefly at the Department of Homeland Security, had been given about a 1% chance of securing the role on Kalshi before the announcement.

  • Prediction markets, where users wager on outcomes ranging from sporting contests to world events, have faced growing scrutiny over the risk of traders profiting from inside information.

  • In July, Trump's teleprompter operator came under investigation by the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission over potential insider trading.

data.title: Lockheed unveils next-gen Patriot interceptor to defend against hypersonic threats
data.description:
Lockheed Martin on Friday unveiled its new PAC-3 Edge missile interceptor, which it said will will add "a revolutionary defensive capability" against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the U.S. military seeks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.

Lockheed said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls, and a ​multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman , enhancing ​the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, ‌and providing greater speed and maneuverability, allowing it to fly at higher altitudes and longer distances than other PAC-3 missiles.

The new interceptor is part of the U.S. Army's Future Interceptor program currently in competition, and builds on Lockheed's PAC-3 MSE, which has been used extensively to defend against missile attacks in Ukraine and Iran.

"The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, Lockheed president of missiles and ​fire control Tim Cahill ⁠told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 ​units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE."

Lockheed said it will advance development and begin testing PAC-3 Edge in 2027 to prepare for rapid deployment by 2031.

data.title: 13D Filings — Barrons.com
data.description:
These disclosures are from 13Ds filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission. 13Ds are filed within 10 days of an entity's attaining more than 5% in any class of a company's securities. Subsequent changes in holdings or intentions must be reported in amended filings. This material is from Oct. 1 through Oct. 7, 2026. Source: VerityData

Activist Filings

Vail Resorts (MTN) DKR Oasis Management raised its stake in the ski resort operator to 3,223,435 shares. Oasis did so through the purchase of 599,523 Vail Resorts shares from Sept. 23 through Sept. 28 at per share prices ranging from $135.81 to $139.81.

The purchases came after Oasis notified Vail Resorts on Sept. 10 of its intent to nominate four director candidates at the 2026 annual meeting, including Robert Chapek and retired Olympic skier Picabo Street. Oasis contends that Vail's valuation relative to peers doesn't fully reflect its portfolio of 42 mountain resorts, and that a reconstituted board would sharpen the company's focus on guest experience, pricing strategy, marketing effectiveness, and fuller use of its hospitality assets.

Following the latest purchases, Oasis continues to own a 9% stake in Vail Resorts' outstanding stock. Shares of Vail Resorts have gained roughly 8.6% in value in 2026.

BrightSpire Capital(BRSP) CWRE SSF Securities Holding filed an initial 13D regarding its stake in the commercial real estate credit REIT, shifting to the stance of an activist investor from previous disclosures in a passive 13G. CWRE SSF Securities Holding reported that it purchased 277,386 BrightSpire Capital shares from July 31 through Sept. 10 at per share prices ranging from $4.49 to $4.97. T

he firm has now asked BrightSpire's board twice to waive the company's 9.8% ownership limit so it could increase its investment, but after the board refused both requests without substantive explanation, CWRE said that it could no longer remain a passive investor while shares trade near all-time lows.

Following the latest purchases, CWRE SSF Securities Holding owns 10,982,257 BrightSpire Capital shares, or 8.7% of those outstanding. Shares of BrightSpire Capital have lost roughly 33.7% of their value in 2026.

Increases in Holdings

Elastic (ESTC) Pictet Asset Management raised its stake in the data analytics software company to 5,445,175 shares. Pictet Asset Management reported that it purchased 257,469 Elastic shares from Sept. 8 through Oct. 5 at per share prices ranging from $83.39 to $94.23, and sold 62,061 shares from Sept. 4 through Oct. 2 at $85.11 to $95.14. Following the latest activity, Pictet Asset Management owns a 5.2% stake in Elastic's outstanding stock. Shares of Elastic have gained roughly 29.7% in value in 2026.

Decreases in Holdings

Navigator Holdings (NVGS) BW Group lowered its stake in the liquefied-gas shipping company to 4,059,078 shares. BW Group did so through the sale of 700,000 Navigator Holdings shares from Sept. 23 through Oct. 1 at per share prices ranging from $22.58 to $23.80. Following the latest sales, BW Group continues to own a 6.6% stake in Navigator Holdings' outstanding stock. Shares of Navigator Holdings have gained about 35.9% in value in 2026.

data.title: Fitch revises Nigeria's outlook to 'positive' on expectations of sustained reforms
data.description:
Credit ratings agency Fitch revised Nigeria's outlook to "positive" from "stable" on Friday, as it expects the government's economic reforms to be continued beyond the 2027 elections.

The agency said recent policy reforms had boosted foreign exchange reserves, supported naira stability and improved the economy's resilience to external shocks.

President Bola Tinubu has overhauled Nigeria's economy since he took over in 2023, implementing subsidy, currency and tax reforms aimed at shoring up public finances, though the measures have fuelled inflation and driven up living costs.

On Thursday, the World Bank said that with inflation easing and poverty gradually declining, the economy of Africa's most populous nation could grow by an average of 4.4% through 2028, if reforms are sustained and service delivery improves.

Despite an improved macroeconomic policy framework, Fitch maintained Nigeria's rating at "B", saying it remained constrained by weak governance indicators, dependence on hydrocarbons, high inflation and security challenges.

In May, peer agency S&P upgraded Nigeria's long-term sovereign rating to "B" on solid economic growth. In August, Moody's revised Nigeria's outlook to "positive", citing its improved ability to withstand external shocks.

data.title: Super Micro contractor pleads guilty in scheme to divert AI servers with Nvidia chips to China
data.description:
By Karen Freifeld

A contractor linked to Super Micro Computer has pleaded guilty in a scheme to illegally export computer servers containing advanced Nvidia AI chips to China, according to a court filing on Friday.

In March, U.S. prosecutors charged Ting-Wei "Willy" Sun and two others associated with Super Micro, including a co-founder, with conspiring to divert about $2.5 billion worth of U.S. AI technology to China in violation of export laws.

The court docket showed Sun entered his guilty plea on Thursday in U.S. District Court in Manhattan.

data.title: Global Compliance Applications Corp. Signs Memorandum of Understanding to Evaluate Blockchain Coupon and Rewards Integration with Instacash in Eswatini
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - October 9, 2026) - Global Compliance Applications Corp. (FSE: TK6) (OTC Pink: FUAPF) (the "Company" or "GCAC") announces that it has entered into a memorandum of understanding on October 9, 2026 (the "MOU") with Directore Technologies (Proprietary) Limited, trading as Instacash ("Instacash"), to evaluate the integration and potential commercialization of GCAC's coupon, rewards and merchant-engagement technology within Instacash's payment and wallet ecosystem in Eswatini.

The MOU establishes a framework for technical, commercial and regulatory due diligence, pilot design and negotiation of definitive agreements. The proposed technology would support merchant coupons, customer rewards, campaign management and redemption analytics while Instacash would retain control of its 220,000 user customer relationships and regulated payment operations. Any proposed blockchain or digital-asset functionality beyond the coupon record would require separate legal and regulatory analysis.

Proposed Commercial Framework

The parties are evaluating a potential technology deployment package with a stated negotiation value of up to US$1,000,000. This amount is a proposed commercial valuation and is not an agreed payment, booked revenue, financing commitment or independently established asset value. The MOU contemplates that consideration, if agreed, could comprise cash, equity or deferred value, revenue participation, or a combination. No final pricing, payment schedule, equity issuance or revenue-sharing terms have been agreed.

The parties also contemplate a staged pilot, with milestones and acceptance criteria to be agreed in a written pilot plan. Any production rollout would depend on satisfactory technical integration, commercial feasibility, data protection, regulatory review, internal approvals and execution of definitive agreements. The MOU does not obligate either party to complete a production deployment or securities transaction.

"We see an opportunity to evaluate how GCAC's coupon and engagement infrastructure can complement an existing African payments ecosystem of 220,000 plus users without displacing its core payment functions," said Ryan Gibson, Chief Executive Officer of GCAC. "Our immediate priority is a disciplined assessment of the technology, economics and regulatory requirements before committing to a commercial rollout. Our goal, is to provide a lucrative advertising and business stream of revenue for the Payment Operator in the spirit of creating an African based super wallet."

Material Terms and Status

The MOU provides for an initial evaluation period, with a six-month term unless extended or terminated under its provisions. Certain provisions, including confidentiality and specified protections, are intended to be binding; the principal commercial arrangements remain subject to definitive documentation. Any equity consideration would require separate agreements, applicable corporate and regulatory approvals, and CSE acceptance where required. No securities are being issued pursuant to the MOU at this time. There can be no assurance that the proposed pilot, deployment or commercial transaction will proceed.

About Global Compliance Applications Corp.

Global Compliance Applications Corp. develops and licenses blockchain-enabled technology solutions, including its Efixii platform and related digital engagement and data-management applications. For further information, visit the Company's corporate website and public disclosure record. (http://www.gcac.tech).
